findings.evidence: The skill automatically identifies your project by scanning for common package files: package.json, go.mod, Cargo.toml, Gemfile, pom.xml, *.csproj
findings.fix: Keep one detection pointer in SKILL.md step 1; the repeated file-to-language list is generic model knowledge, so move the README Language-Agnostic Detection list to references/ only if users ask for it and record the removal

findings.evidence: A lockfile generated by another package manager or version may silently alter the resolved graph and make builds irreproducible
findings.fix: Drop this bullet from Non-obvious failure modes: the NEVER list already states the same rule with its reason, and the remaining four bullets carry the environment-specific gotchas

findings.evidence: description names Node, Python, Go, Rust, Ruby, Java, and .NET but not the manifest keywords package.json, pyproject.toml, go.mod, Cargo.toml, Gemfile, pom.xml or csproj
findings.fix: Audit, diagnose, and conservatively update project dependencies and lockfiles for Node (package.json), Python (pyproject.toml, requirements.txt, Pipfile), Go (go.mod), Rust (Cargo.toml), Ruby (Gemfile), Java (pom.xml, build.gradle), and .NET (csproj). Auto-applies safe minor and patch updates after a recoverable snapshot, with tests and a security audit per cohort, and asks before every major, 0.x or prerelease change. Use when asked to update dependencies, update the safe ones automatically, find outdated packages, resolve dependency conflicts, or remediate vulnerable packages, even when the user only names a lockfile or a failing install. Not for runtime upgrades, package publishing, or Renovate configuration.

findings.evidence: "$SKILL/scripts/run-taze.sh" and "Run in monorepo mode ... run-taze.sh -r" with no --include or workspace confirmation
findings.fix: Point the README Node.js example at SKILL.md's scoped order: a scan is scripts/run-taze.sh major, and a write needs --include plus --no-github-actions --no-node-version, with -r only after the workspace is confirmed; keep the skill-directory resolution note

findings.evidence: By default edit the target versions directly in the manifest. Alternatively run a scoped taze write, only in a disposable copy
findings.fix: Make the direct manifest edit the only default for an exact target map, and gate the disposable-copy taze write on the case where the mode's latest version equals that map; the current or leaves two equal write paths for a fragile lockfile change

findings.evidence: 11 should-trigger and 10 should-not-trigger queries, but the negatives are easy neighbours (Renovate, Node.js itself, publish to npm) and none is a near-miss such as adding one named dependency or editing an application that merely imports a package
findings.fix: Replace four weak negatives with near-misses that mention a manifest or a package but ask for a feature, a new dependency, or a code fix, and add one casual should-trigger query that names only a failing lockfile

findings.evidence: Security scanners are ecosystem-specific: govulncheck ./..., cargo audit, bundle-audit check ... mvn org.owasp:dependency-check-maven:check
findings.fix: Split the scanner sentence into one invocation per ecosystem and say each is run only after that ecosystem is confirmed, matching the Node and Python commands already gated in their own files; an agent on a Go task otherwise has five unrelated commands in one line
